subject: Unexpected June overage — request for usage heatmap and reconciliation
messages:
From: Pulse Analytics <billing@pulseanalytics.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: June invoice — sudden 42% increase, need reconciliation

Hi Rohan,

We just received the June invoice and it shows a 42% jump vs May (line item: usage tokens / embeddings). We run a steady workload; there was no product change or big campaign on our side. Please send a per-hour usage heatmap for the month, an explanation for the spike, and an initial proposal for remediation/credit while you investigate.

Attached is a short sample export from our side (pulse-usage-sample.csv) showing the client-side call timestamps.

This is blocking our finance team from approving payment — can we get first response today?

Thanks,
Elena Suarez
Head of Finance, Pulse Analytics
billing@pulseanalytics.com

--
Attachment: pulse-usage-sample.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Pulse Analytics <billing@pulseanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: June invoice — sudden 42% increase, need reconciliation

Elena — thanks for the note and the sample. Sorry for the surprise. I’m pulling a per-hour heatmap and the raw request logs from our metering pipeline now.

Quick ask while we investigate: can you confirm whether the sample file includes requests from your staging/dev keys or only production keys? We’ve seen cases where test jobs were accidentally run under prod credentials and they look identical in invoices. If you don’t see staging in your sample, we’ll still provide a detailed prefix/embedding-level breakdown.

I’m looping in Ben (billing ops) and Monica (customer success) to coordinate evidence and a mitigation proposal. We’ll aim to send a preliminary reconciliation and a proposed credit within 48 hours.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Accounts Lead, Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

--
(no attachments)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Pulse Analytics <billing@pulseanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: June invoice — sudden 42% increase, need reconciliation

Elena / Rohan — initial findings from a quick sample of our telemetry: we see three distinct bursts on 2027-06-07 at 02:00–03:00 UTC, 2027-06-14 at 18:00–19:30 UTC, and 2027-06-20 at 04:30–05:15 UTC. In the traces during those windows there are duplicated requests with identical request IDs originating from the same IP block — looks like a client-side retry loop that replayed previously cached requests.

I’ve attached the filtered server logs for those windows (redwood-sample-logs.zip) and a small SQL snippet we ran to count request id collisions. We’ll produce the per-hour heatmap CSV shortly.

Ben Carter
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

--
Attachment: redwood-sample-logs.zip (filtered logs, ~250KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Pulse Analytics <billing@pulseanalytics.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-28T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: June invoice — sudden 42% increase, need reconciliation

Hi Elena — thanks for the sample and Ben for the quick triage.

We ran a correlation between your CSV and our logs — ~18% of the billed requests in the three burst windows appear to be direct duplicates (same payload and request_id seen >1 in a 30s window). Our proposed remediation: we will issue a one-time credit equal to the duplicate-request portion of June usage (calculated as the deduplicated token count) while you investigate the root cause on your side.

If that’s acceptable we’ll draft a short credit memo (pdf) and have Finance post the credit to your account; for immediate unblock we can provisionally reduce the outstanding invoice by the credit amount and give Pulse 14 days to confirm. Please confirm if you want us to proceed with the provisional reduction.

Also, to help prevent recurrence: we recommend your engineering team add idempotency checks on the client side for long-running jobs and rotate any keys that were used during the migration window. Happy to jump on a quick 30-min call if helpful.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

--
Attachment: proposed-credit-memo.pdf (draft, 8KB)

From: Elena Suarez <elena@pulseanalytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T15:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: June invoice — sudden 42% increase, need reconciliation

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what our engineering team found (a migration job accidentally ran using prod credentials and a retry wrapper re-submitted a subset of batches). We appreciate the proposed credit.

Please proceed with the provisional invoice reduction and attach the credit memo to the account. Also please open a JIRA incident (we noted JIRA-INC-7392 in your related links) so our procurement team has a ticket for audit. We’ll rotate the affected keys and confirm in writing when that’s complete.

Two quick logistics questions:
1) What will the timeline be for posting the credit to the account and reflecting it on the next invoice?
2) If we end up needing a formal refund (vs credit), what is Redwood’s process / lead time?

If you prefer, we can do a 20-min sync tomorrow morning PT to close this out.

Best,
Elena
Head of Finance, Pulse Analytics

--
(End of thread)
